The [official PyTorch port](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch) implements gSASRec through training changes. With N real items, α=K/(N−1), β=1−t+tα; therefore K=32, t=0.75 gives β=0.25+24/(N−1). K=32 is a custom choice; the authors recommend K=256, t=0.75. Exact positive-logit transformation: γ(s)=−log(σ(s)^(−β)−1), equivalently −log(expm1(β·softplus(−s))). Negative logits remain unchanged. The [training implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/train_gsasrec.py) computes the transformation in float64 with probability/intermediate clamps, applies BCEWithLogits elementwise, averages over all K+1 candidates, then averages over valid sequence positions. Algebraically, the unclipped loss is [β·softplus(−s_positive)+Σ softplus(s_negative)]/(K+1). Separately averaging positive and negative losses changes their relative weighting.

The [official sampler](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/dataset_utils.py) uses independent torch.randint draws over IDs 1…N: uniform sampling with replacement, allowing duplicates, the target positive, and items from the user’s history. It nevertheless computes α using N−1. Thus the port’s sampler and the paper’s non-positive sampling denominator differ slightly. Inference from this implementation: rejecting user-history items changes the negative distribution and the calibration assumptions; retaining α=K/(N−1) does not correct that change. For reproducibility, explicitly distinguish reproducing the official sampler from retaining RecHarness history exclusions. The latter can be evaluated as a controlled gBCE variant, but should not be described as exact reproduction of the official sampling/calibration setup.
